item.title: Israeli financial news outlet reveals €150 million warship deal with Cyprus
item.description: According to the Israeli financial newspaper Calcalist, an agreement is expected to be signed in the coming weeks, once the terms are finalised between the defence ministries of Israel and Cyprus.

item.title: Trump envoy Witkoff to meet Zelenskyy in Oslo before planned Putin talks in Moscow
item.description: The latest diplomatic push comes amid a deepening rift between Kyiv and Washington, as the US presses Ukraine to halt strikes on Russian oil infrastructure while Kyiv faces delays in Patriot missile deliveries and reported restrictions on intelligence-sharing and satellite communications.

item.title: At least five killed and thousands evacuated as Storm Adam batters eastern Spain
item.description: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez will visit Valencia on Tuesday to see the impact of the storm.

item.title: Ukraine carries out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line
item.description: Ukraine’s 92nd Assault Brigade says it has carried out its first aerial drone evacuation of a wounded soldier, pulling him from a position where mines and Russian drone activity made a conventional rescue impossible.

item.title: Oil prices top $110 as traders weigh Middle East supply risks
item.description: The price of Brent crude remained at a five-month high as uncertainty over when energy supplies will return to normal amid the war with Iran keeps oil inflated.

item.title: With 29 designated Cittaslow cities, Türkiye is leading the way in slow travel
item.description: The Cittaslow’ initiative has been highlighting the lesser-known burgs around the world which celebrate local food, culture and history. Türkiye is the proud owner of 29 such towns, all offering unfettered access to myriad aspects of Turkish culture.

item.title: Pop culture iconography as protest: Why has the One Piece skull been adopted by French protesters?
item.description: Pop culture as expression of revolt: Gen Z have adopted a symbol from a popular manga for their protest movements. Here’s why the One Piece flag has become a recognised symbol of revolt during French protests - and beyond.

item.title: Ryanair CEO calls EU chief Ursula von der Leyen 'useless' and demands tax on US and Chinese airlines
item.description: Ryanair is cutting a million seats from Belgium this winter as Michael O’Leary warns of steep fare rises in 2027 and demands foreign airlines pay their share.

item.title: Spain versus Morocco: this is how the military forces of both countries stand in 2026
item.description: Spain spends three times more on defence than Morocco and leads in air and naval power, but Rabat has more troops and rockets. US-backed rearmament boosts its strength and narrows the gap.

item.title: France presses resale platforms to remove 'stolen' goods after unrest
item.description: France's digital minister on Monday urged online resale platforms to remove listings for "stolen items" following Saturday's looting and summoned representatives of companies including Vinted and eBay for talks.

item.title: France to impose new curfews where 'situation requires it', PM Lecornu says
item.description: Under pressure, the government scheduled another series of emergency meetings on Tuesday, including talks involving representatives of major social media platforms.

item.title: Protests in France: Russian interference "quite certain" says French politician
item.description: French poltician Patrick Molinoz, vice-president of the French Mayoral Association claims that recent violence in France was "planned", citing a "certain" Russian intereference.

item.title: Police patrol Paris streets under overnight curfew
item.description: Paris police imposed an overnight curfew on Monday around Place de la Republique and Les Halles after France’s worst rioting in years. Streets were calm.

item.title: At least 14 killed and seven injured in landslide at illegal gold mine in Colombia
item.description: Armed groups in Narino, an illegal mining hotspot on the border with Ecuador, control the clandestine gold trade as well as trafficking drugs and engaging in extortion.

item.title: Ryanair CEO calls Commission President Ursula von der Leyen 'useless'
item.description: Michael O’Leary, CEO of Irish airline Ryanair, has criticised European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s green policies, arguing that they add “complexity and cost”. He also branded the European Parliament a “ship of fools”, claiming its green laws are driving up the cost of air travel.

item.title: Trump says Paris will soon be 'a Muslim city' under Macron's immigration policies
item.description: US President Donald Trump says he warned French President Emmanuel Macron that he was making "a big mistake" by allowing immigrants into France

item.title: ‘Albertans chose Canada’: Carney hails vote to reject referendum
item.description: Separatist leaders vow to fight on, warning the province’s governing party could split over the issue.

item.title: Inflation squeeze pushes Europeans onto the streets. Can the EU help?
item.description: Euro-area inflation climbed to 3.8%, its highest in recent months, and Europeans are taking to the streets to demand relief from soaring energy, food and housing costs. Watch the video.

item.title: Pressure mounts on Macron as France reels from unrest
item.description: Hello from Brussels. I’m Mared Gwyn, holding the newsletter pen once again today. In this edition: what the unrest in France means for its embattled president, and the latest from Ukraine amid signs of intensified diplomacy.

item.title: Planning a Christmas getaway? Here’s where flights and hotels could cost less
item.description: From the best days to fly to the destinations seeing price drops on hotels, this is where you should be headed for Christmas in 2026, according to a new KAYAK study.

item.title: Residents clean up as deadly floods devastate eastern Spain
item.description: Residents of Els Poblets, near Alicante, cleared mud and wrecked furniture on Monday after floods in eastern Spain left at least two people dead.

item.title: Europe Today: Blame continues in France, Russia kills two children in Kharkiv
item.description: Blame in France over protests continues as Sébastien Lecornu accuses the ultra-left of orchestrating the unrest. In Kharkiv, two children are among the victims of a Russian strike on a park as Putin reportedly floats a summit without Kyiv. And an interview with Ryanair CEO Michael O’Leary.

item.title: France's traditional smoked sausage under threat – but is Brussels really to blame?
item.description: Political parties across Brittany are up in arms over the French government's failure to defend andouille de Guémené, a traditional sausage suspected of posing a cancer risk.

item.title: US allegedly holding up delivery of Patriot air defence missiles, Zelenskyy says
item.description: Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured over military aid and intelligence sharing, with Zelenskyy saying that Ukraine received no warning of Russian missile strikes that targeted energy facilities in the capital region.

item.title: Researchers use ChatGPT-style technology to predict stroke risk from a person’s DNA
item.description: A new AI tool that identifies genetic risk factors for stroke could open the door to more personalised prevention and treatment.

item.title: Egyptian cucumber farmer helps archaeologists find giant Ramses II statue fragments
item.description: A farmer’s discovery has led to the remains of two colossal royal statues and ancient inscriptions in Egypt’s Nile Delta. Archaeologists have identified one as Ramses II and are investigating how the finds fit into the area’s history.

item.title: How planting a 'rain garden' could help protect your home from flooding
item.description: Flooding is expected to grow more extreme due to climate change. Your garden could be your home's first defence.

item.title: These are Europe’s cosiest cities to travel to this autumn, according to a new ranking
item.description: From Bruges’ fairytale streets to Lisbon’s sun-soaked cafés, these European cities are perfect for a cosy autumn escape.

item.title: Ukraine needs another €70 billion, but where will the EU find the money?
item.description: The EU is searching for another €70 billion to sustain Ukraine's war effort in 2027, but rising borrowing costs and divisions over the Russian assets leave Brussels with few easy options.

item.title: Trump says he is ready to meet Putin and Xi in China
item.description: Trump also renewed his criticism of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy saying it was "time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine."

item.title: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines hurt in car attack loses leg, media say
item.description: Haines was hit by a Toyota Land Cruiser outside her office in the town of Wangaratta, just over 200 kilometres northeast of Melbourne, at around 0635 CET on Monday.

item.title: Japan launches unprecedented mission to bring back samples from Mars' moon Phobos
item.description: NASA has landed nine spacecraft on Mars over the past 50 years, and China touched down in 2021, but no one has returned samples from Mars, let alone its moons.

item.title: Why pharma giant Roche is putting German investments on hold
item.description: Germany’s bid to revive its struggling economy faces a fresh setback as a major pharmaceutical player raises concerns over the country’s business climate.

item.title: France's riot damage doubles: How will businesses pay for the destruction?
item.description: At least 3,000 French shops were hit over the weekend. Insurers say they are mobilised, but lost trade may not be covered. Here is who pays the riot bill.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang warns Germany is falling behind in AI race
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Huang are set to unveil a joint AI pact intended to speed up the integration of AI products across German industry.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV holds call with Zelenskyy, Vatican says
item.description: Chicago-born Leo, 71, has been calling for a humanitarian truce in Oleshky, a city under Russian siege, to allow food and medical aid to arrive and for civilians to be evacuated safely.

item.title: Video: Priest dies after cross falls on him during Mass in Ecuador
item.description: Ecuadorian priest Patricio Sánchez died after a large cross fell on him while he was celebrating Mass in the city of Guayaquil.

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo suspended for 30 days after quitting Portugal camp
item.description: On 30 September, the former Real Madrid and Manchester United star walked out of an international camp before a training session at Parken Stadium in Copenhagen.

item.title: Deadly floods sweep through eastern Spain after torrential rain
item.description: Torrential rain triggered severe flooding in eastern Spain, sweeping away cars, submerging roads and leaving at least four people dead.

item.title: Rubio puts Trans-Caspian trade and critical minerals at centre of Central Asia talks
item.description: The US and five Central Asian governments backed closer transport and industrial cooperation at a C5+1 meeting in Samarkand. Rubio also held bilateral talks, while Uzbekistan signed the Artemis Accords.

item.title: Lavrov backs Iran, hours after Trump says Russia doing 'very little' to help Tehran
item.description: Just hours after Trump publicly claimed Russia was doing “little” to help Iran, Moscow reaffirmed its full support for Tehran, with Foreign Minister Lavrov describing Iran's fight as a "just cause."

item.title: 'How are we supposed to recover?': Shopkeepers react to looting and destruction across France
item.description: French shopkeepers are struggling to come to terms with the destruction left by a night of rioting and looting, with some fearing for the future of their businesses and employees.

item.title: Albanian PM Rama accuses anti-government protesters of crossing 'red line' amid violent demonstrations
item.description: The European Commission released a statement condemning the violence in Albania on Sunday, saying it had "no place in a democratic society" and that the response "must remain within the law and proportionate."

item.title: Macron increasingly isolated amid unrest across France
item.description: Saturday’s violent protests and looting across France have deepened Macron’s political isolation, raising questions over his authority.

item.title: Trump signs order aimed at boosting women’s health research
item.description: United States President Donald Trump signed an executive order establishing two bodies to boost women’s health research, address gaps in medical knowledge and improve prevention, diagnosis and treatment.

item.title: Dutch PM Rob Jetten and partner expecting child via surrogate mother: 'Someone very special is on the way'
item.description: "Being a surrogate mother feels like a very special way to help make our dear friends’ dream come true," Lisa, the surrogate mother, was quoted as saying.

item.title: Qatar plans new defence partnership and warns of energy crisis 'peak'
item.description: Qatar is preparing a new regional defence partnership while keeping channels open with Tehran, arguing that dialogue and economic ties offer a route to lasting peace. Doha also warned of an energy disruption “peak” with more difficulties on the horizon “in the coming days and months”.

item.title: EU Parliament leaders set for re-election despite cracks in centrist alliance
item.description: Manfred Weber, Iratxe García Pérez and Valérie Hayer are expected to be re-elected unopposed, even as growing tensions threaten the centrist alliance supporting Ursula von der Leyen.
